newsitem.title: UK: Bulgaria is front runner in emerging debt market.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria is front runner in emerging debt market.

text.p: Emerging debt prices were firm on Monday, with Bulgaria taking the lead.
Activity was fairly subdued ahead of the noon market closure for a U.S. holiday.
"There's been a little bit of movement this morning, mainly in Bulgaria," a European bank trader said.
IABs were bid up to a point higher at 52-5/8 cents in the dollar.
Traders said the strength, which one found surprising, had more to do with investors looking for high yield in a generally bullish market than any particular improvement in Bulgaria's own situation.
"I think Bulgaria will be all right in the end, but they have got to walk a nasty, rocky road over the next few weeks," one trader said.

Paribas, in a research report, recommended investors look at being overweight in Bulgarian Bradys to exploit a likely strong rise once there is an agreement with the International Monetary Fund and establishment of a currency board.

"Provided that (a) new government then clearly commits to a comprehensive reform programme -- we view this as likely -- the threat of default through June on external debt obligations remains low," Paribas said.
Elsewhere there was some activity in Latin America which remains strong.
Russia was also firmer, helped by reports that President Boris Yeltsin's health was improving.
Local media reports quoted Kremlin sources as saying Yeltsin would be out of hospital on Tuesday but there was no official confirmation.
